'''Kyle Collinsworth''' (born October 3, 1991) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for [[Brigham Young University]] (BYU). During the 2014–15 season, Collinsworth broke the NCAA single-season record for triple-doubles with six, which also tied the NCAA career record.<ref>{{cite news|title=Collinsworth ties record with 6th triple-double; BYU wins|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/03/10/ap-bkc-wcc-portland-byu|publisher=Sports Illustrated|date=March 10, 2015|access-date=March 10, 2015}}</ref> On March 16, 2016, Collinsworth recorded his twelfth career triple-double, extending the NCAA record he set earlier in the season.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Call|title=Collinsworth records another triple-double in BYU's win over Portland|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865648676/BYU-basketball-Collinsworths-11th-triple-double-pushes-Cougars-past-Portland.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20160807102646/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865648676/BYU-basketball-Collinsworths-11th-triple-double-pushes-Cougars-past-Portland.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 7, 2016|publisher=Deseret News|date=February 25, 2016|access-date=February 25, 2016}}</ref>

==High school career==
Born in [[Provo, Utah]], Collinsworth attended [[Provo High School]], where he was a four-year starter and played for teams that won two 4A state titles. He was three times named to the first-team all-state team. As a senior, he averaged 23.7 points, 10.8 rebounds, 8.3 assists, 4.0 steals, and 2.0 blocks per game and recorded five triple-doubles.<ref name=MaxPreps>{{cite web|title=Kyle Collinsworth's Basketball Stats|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/kyle-collinsworth/7wNkjfTqEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/gendersport/basketball-stats.htm|website=MaxPreps.com|access-date=March 10, 2015}}</ref> He was Deseret News Mr. Basketball, Salt Lake Tribune Male Athlete of the Year and Utah Gatorade Player of the Year. He was also selected to play in the 2010 High School Academic All-American Classic.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jim|last=Rayburn|title=Mr. Basketball: Provo's Kyle Collinsworth deemed best of the best|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/700016778/Mr-Basketball-Provos-Kyle-Collinsworth-deemed-best-of-the-best.html?pg=all|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402175747/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/700016778/Mr-Basketball-Provos-Kyle-Collinsworth-deemed-best-of-the-best.html?pg=all|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 2, 2015|publisher=Deseret News|date=March 16, 2010|access-date=March 10, 2015}}</ref>

Collinsworth was recruited by [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|ASU]], [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]], Cal, [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], Gonzaga, Kansas, [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], Utah, Utah State, [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], and Washington State.<ref name=KSL>{{cite news|title=Collinsworth signs national letter of intent with BYU|url=http://www.ksl.com/?sid=8651218|publisher=KSL|date=November 12, 2009|access-date=March 10, 2015}}</ref> He committed to play college basketball at BYU and signed his letter of intent on November 12, 2009.<ref name="KSL" />

==College career==
===Freshman year===
As a freshman, Collinsworth averaged 5.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.1 steals while shooting .481 from the field, .259 from three and .568 from the free throw line.  He posted season highs of 16 points, 15 rebounds, 6 assists, 4 steals and 3 blocks and recorded 1 double-double.  He posted 15 rebounds against Florida in the NCAA Tournament. Following his freshman season, Collinsworth departed on a two-year LDS mission to Russia.

===Sophomore year===
Following his LDS mission, Collinsworth was readmitted to BYU and was named as a team captain for the 2013–14 season. As a sophomore, he averaged 14.0 points, 8.1 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.7 steals and recorded 7 double-doubles. He ranked second in the WCC in rebounding (83rd in the nation), third in steals (89th nationally), and third in assists (60th nationally). He was one of only four players in the country to be ranked in the top 100 in assists and steals. Collinsworth was named to the All-WCC First Team, the WCC All-Tournament Team, and the CollegeSportsMadness.com All-WCC Third Team.

===Junior year===
In his junior year, Collinsworth averaged 13.5 points, 8.7 rebounds, 5.9 assists per game, and set an NCAA single-season record of six triple-doubles. That also tied an NCAA record for career triple-doubles, joining former [[Drexel University|Drexel]] guard Michael Anderson and past [[LSU]] superstar center [[Shaquille O'Neal]].  Collinsworth was the only player in the nation who ranked in the top 100 nationally in rebounds (42nd), assists (16th), and steals (71st) per game.  He ranked second in the WCC in each category, and was again named All-WCC First Team and WCC All-Tournament Team at the end of the season.

===Senior year===
On February 1, 2016, Collinsworth was named one of 10 finalists for the Bob Cousy Point Guard of the Year Award.<ref>{{cite news|first=Matt|last=Nortlander|title=Cat Barber, Fred VanVleet missing from list of Cousy Award finalists|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25468790/cat-barber-fred-vanvleet-conspicuously-missing-from-cousy-award-finalists|access-date=February 2, 2016|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=February 1, 2016}}</ref> For the season, he averaged 15.3 points, 8.2 rebounds, and 7.4 assists per game - ranking 5th in the nation in the latter. With a triple-double against [[UAB Blazers|UAB]], he tied his own single-season record for triple doubles with six, and extended his NCAA record for career triple doubles to 12, which still stands today in NCAA men's basketball. (In women's play, [[Sabrina Ionescu]] had 26 for [[Oregon Ducks women's basketball|Oregon]] from 2016 to 2020.) He led his team to the NIT final four,<ref name="cbs">{{cite web|first=Chip|last=Patterson|title=2016 NIT bracket, schedule, tip times: Valparaiso-BYU set for semifinals|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25516048/nit-bracket-schedule-tip-times-florida-st-marys-into-quarterfinals|website=CBS Sports|date=March 24, 2016|access-date=March 29, 2016}}</ref> although the NCAA ordered the NIT appearance and all but one of BYU's wins in that season vacated due to findings that BYU boosters had provided improper benefits to Collinsworth's teammate Nick Emery.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25226997/ncaa-committee-infractions-says-byu-cougars-vacate-47-wins-lose-scholarship |title=NCAA committee on infractions penalizes BYU in Nick Emery infractions case |first=Myron |last=Medcalf |website=ESPN.com |date=November 9, 2018 |access-date=November 24, 2018}}</ref><ref name="Emery decision">{{cite web|url=https://ncaaorg.s3.amazonaws.com/enforcement/infractions/decisions/Nov2018INF_BYUPublicInfractionsDecision.pdf |title=Brigham Young University Public Infractions Decision |publisher=NCAA |date=November 9, 2018 |access-date=November 24, 2018}}</ref>{{efn|Collinsworth's triple-double record was not affected by this NCAA action. The only season in which Collinsworth played that was affected by NCAA sanctions was his senior season of 2015–16, and the NCAA's official decision specified that Emery was the only player who would have any records vacated in that season. Specifically, Page 15 of the decision stated that "...the individual finishes and any awards for all eligible student-athletes shall be retained."<ref name="Emery decision"/>}} For his efforts, Collinsworth was named WCC Player of the Year, and again repeated as All-WCC First Team (for the third season in a row). He was also named Honorable Mention All-American by several media organizations, including the [[Associated Press]].

==Professional career==
===Texas Legends (2016–2018)===
After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Collinsworth joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Bobby|last=Karalla|url=http://www.mavs.com/2016-mavericks-orlando-summer-league-roster/|title=2016 Mavericks Orlando Summer League Roster|work=Mavs.com|date=June 29, 2016|access-date=October 19, 2016}}</ref> On July 21, 2016, he signed with the Mavericks,<ref>{{cite web|first=Arya|last=Ahmadi|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-guard-kyle-collinsworth/|title=Mavericks sign guard Kyle Collinsworth|work=Mavs.com|date=July 21, 2016|access-date=July 21, 2016}}</ref> but was waived on October 22 after appearing in five preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|first=Bobby|last=Karalla|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-request-waivers-five-set-opening-night-roster/|title=Mavericks request waivers on five, set opening night roster|work=Mavs.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023140647/http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-request-waivers-five-set-opening-night-roster/|archive-date=October 23, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On October 30, 2016, he was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]] of the NBA Development League, now known as the [[NBA G League]], as an affiliate player of the Mavericks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://texas.dleague.nba.com/news/legends-announce-2016-training-camp-roster/|title=Legends Announce Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 30, 2016|access-date=November 4, 2016}}</ref>

On March 30, 2017, Collinsworth was waived by the Legends.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Texas-Legends/32/Transaction_History/|title=Texas Legends Transactions History|work=RealGM.com|access-date=March 1, 2017}}</ref> He was then reacquired by the Legends for their 2017 training camp.

===Salt Lake City Stars (2019–2020)===
Collinsworth was added to the opening night roster of the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stars Finalize Opening Night Roster |url=https://saltlakecity.gleague.nba.com/news/stars-finalize-opening-night-roster-2/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 9, 2019 |date=November 8, 2019 |archive-date=November 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191112054606/https://saltlakecity.gleague.nba.com/news/stars-finalize-opening-night-roster-2/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 18, 2020, Collinsworth scored 16 points, grabbed 15 rebounds and dished out seven assists in a loss to the [[Westchester Knicks]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Kyle Collinsworth: Registers double-double Saturday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kyle-collinsworth-registers-double-double-saturday/ |access-date=June 2, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 19, 2020}}</ref> He sat out with an unspecified illness between January 24 and February 19.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kyle Collinsworth: Sits out with undisclosed issue |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kyle-collinsworth-sits-out-with-undisclosed-issue/ |access-date=June 2, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 1, 2020}}</ref>

===SeaHorses Mikawa (2020–2022)===
On October 9, 2020, the [[SeaHorses Mikawa]] announced that they had signed with Collinsworth.<ref>{{cite web|title=選手加入のお知らせ(カイル・コリンズワース 選手)|url=https://go-seahorses.jp/news/detail/id=16181|language=ja|date=October 9, 2020|website=go-seahorses.jp|access-date=October 9, 2020}}</ref>

===San-en NeoPhoenix (2022–2023)===
On July 1, 2022, the [[San-en NeoPhoenix]] announced that Collinsworth is part of the team for the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=2022-23シーズン 三遠ネオフェニックス ロスター決定のお知らせ)|url=https://www.neophoenix.jp/news/detail/id=18293|language=ja|date=July 1, 2022|website=neophoenix.jp|access-date=July 1, 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Collinsworth served as a [[Missionary (LDS Church)|missionary]] for [[the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] for two years (2011–2012) in [[Russia]] between his freshman and sophomore years of college. He is married to Shea Martinez-Collinsworth, an [[All-America#Track and field|All-American]] 800m runner on the [[BYU Cougars|BYU]] track team. Together they started the blog {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20180412145528/http://athletesguide5.com/ Athlete's Guide 5]}}, which gave advice to youth about improving athletic performance through 2018 when it became defunct. His older brother, Chris, played for BYU Men's Basketball, but his playing career was cut short due to injuries.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|title=Kyle Collinsworth|url=http://byucougars.com/athlete/m-basketball/kyle-collinsworth|website=BYUCougars.com|access-date=March 10, 2015}}</ref>
